name: Ironpass AcidSeal Chrome-Wrap Rain Sleeve — Pair
description: Fitted over-sleeves in matte black vulcanized polymer designed specifically to sheath chrome arms and exposed spinal conduits during Shelf and Circuit acid rainfall. Fastens with industrial compression snaps along the inner seam. Lightweight, unobtrusive, and purpose-built — popular among aug-users who can't afford full corrosion-resistant chrome upgrades.
functionality: Full acid-rain barrier for exposed chrome limbs; compression-sealed edges prevent seepage at shoulder and wrist joints.
what_it_says: This person has chrome worth protecting and the practicality to do it without spending a fortune.
story_hooks: The left sleeve was split cleanly by something sharp — the owner patched it with electrical tape and won't say what happened.
A batch of counterfeits has been circulating that look identical but dissolve in Grade-3 acid rainfall within minutes.

physical_description.visual_profile: Form-fitting tubular sheaths that extend from shoulder to wrist, hugging the contours of augmented limbs with a sleek, utilitarian aesthetic. The matte black finish creates a seamless visual extension of chrome prosthetics, appearing almost like a second skin layer. Silhouette is streamlined and athletic, emphasizing the augmented anatomy beneath.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fit throughout, snug against the arm without restricting movement. Designed to accommodate varying chrome arm profiles and cybernetic installations. Stretches slightly at the shoulder for donning ease, then locks into place via interior snaps.
physical_description.primary_material: Vulcanized polymer composite — acid-resistant synthetic rubber infused with trace graphene for durability and thermal regulation. Lightweight yet durable enough to withstand chemical precipitation.
physical_description.texture: Smooth matte finish with subtle grip texture on the interior palm side. Surface has a slightly tacky, non-slip quality designed to prevent slippage during rain exposure. Minimal seam visibility on outer surface.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal black throughout, with minimal branding. Occasional silver reinforcement stitching visible along the compression snap line. No patterns or accent colors — purely functional design.
physical_description.closures: Industrial-grade compression snaps arranged vertically along the inner seam (wrist to elbow), allowing quick one-handed fastening and removal. Snaps are oversized and spaced for durability.
distinctive_features: Interior chemical-resistant coating rated for Shelf and Circuit acid precipitation
Reinforced palm and finger webbing for grip stability
Micro-perforations along forearm for thermal breathability without compromising protection
Snap design allows independent adjustment for custom chrome limb geometries
Ironpass utility branding embossed (not printed) on upper shoulder — designed to resist chemical erosion
Universal fit sizing with internal stretch zones
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Affordable protective gear for working-class aug-users. Signals economic pragmatism rather than wealth — buying protection instead of premium chrome.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by industrial workers, street technicians, circuit runners, and aug-users navigating acid rain zones without full-body corrosion protection. Marks the wearer as someone with installed augmentations who operates in hazardous environments. Visible sign of precarity and adaptation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically shows wear within 3-6 months — slight discoloration from acid exposure, micro-tears at snap points from repeated fastening, faint etching patterns on the surface from chemical contact. Patched or reinforced versions are common in long-term users.

Model's chrome limb gleams beneath the protective sheath, snaps and texture details sharp and visible.
